# Independent audit: common-level concurrent cap tightening


`candidate d2f8ecd6d2f1309c`.


ordinary cap-cover reduction, not the unresolved concurrent overlap
inequality or a mixed-integer descent argument. The audit is analytic;
no numerical premise is used.

## 1. Linear algebra and closed-cover criterion

The assumptions imply that the map U:x -> (u_i.x) has rank m-1 and
image rho-perp. All rho_i are strictly positive. The complement of
the union of the CLOSED caps is Ux<b coordinatewise. If rho.b<=0,
this is impossible because rho.Ux=0. If rho.b>0, the vector

    b-c(1,...,1),  c=(rho.b)/(sum rho_i)>0,

lies in rho-perp and is strictly below b in every coordinate, so is
the image of an omitted point. Thus the cover condition is exactly
rho.b<=0. Concurrency is exactly rho.b=0, since this is precisely
the criterion that b itself belong to the image of U. This verifies
both directions, including the equality and closed-boundary cases.

## 2. Inverse cap volumes and attained concurrent level

Every cap-volume function is continuous on its entire support
interval, and strictly decreasing on the open interval: an open
slab between two interior support values contains an interior point
of the full-dimensional convex body and a positive-volume ball.
The unique inverse Q_i:(0,V)->(l_i,h_i) is consequently continuous,
strictly decreasing, and tends to h_i at volume zero.

For a_i(t)=min(A_i,t), the weighted threshold sum

    s(t)=sum rho_i Q_i(a_i(t))

is continuous, and strictly decreases as t increases on
(0,max A_i]. Indeed an index whose original cap volume is max A_i
strictly changes its inverse threshold on every nonempty subinterval
there. At max A_i its value is nonpositive. At zero its limiting
value is strictly positive: for any interior x_0, each
h_i>u_i.x_0, so sum rho_i h_i>0. There is therefore a UNIQUE
root t_* in (0,max A_i]. The root equals max A_i exactly when the
original planes were concurrent. Otherwise t_*<max A_i.

The new thresholds are at least the original thresholds and are
proper, since every a_i(t_*) lies in (0,V). Their weighted sum is
zero, so the new planes intersect and the new closed caps cover
all of R^d. In particular there is no unattained zero-volume
limiting cap hidden in this construction.

## 3. Functional monotonicity and strictness

Let a=min A_i and F(t)=sum min(A_i,t)-r min_i min(A_i,t).
For t>=a its minimum term is the fixed number a. On every
nonempty interval below max A_i at least one summand min(A_i,t)
strictly increases with t, so F strictly increases there. For
0<t<=a,

    F(t)=(m-r)t,

which is strictly increasing because r<m. The formulas agree at
t=a. Thus F is strictly increasing throughout (0,max A_i], not
merely nondecreasing. It follows that F(t_*)<=F(max A_i), with
strict inequality exactly when the starting planes are not
concurrent. This directly checks the delicate r>1 case without
any coordinatewise monotonicity assertion.

## 4. Transfer, zero/full caps, and coefficient range

If the concurrent inequality is F>=V, tightening gives
F(original)>=F(tightened)>=V. If any original A_i=0, the desired
inequality reduces to sum A_i>=V, which is the union bound for
the actual cover of K. If some A_j=V, then

    sum A_i-V=sum_(i!=j) A_i >=(m-1) min A_i
                                      >=r min A_i

for the stated range 0<=r<=m-1. These arguments include simultaneous
zero/full cases. For proper caps, equality after transfer forces
concurrency because the tightening is otherwise strict.

For m=d+1 and gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d, r=m-1/gamma_d satisfies
0<=r<=m-1. The upper bound follows from gamma_d<=1. For the
lower bound, d=1 is equality r=0. For d>=2,
(1+1/d)^d<sum_(j>=0)1/j!<3<=d+1; the strict elementary middle
bound follows, for example, from j!>=2^(j-1) for j>=1, with
strict inequality for j>=3. Hence 1/gamma_d<=d+1.

No claim about the still-unproved concurrent full-rank inequality
has been inferred from this reduction. No correction to the source
was needed.
